analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING 1) Connecting you to GS, 2) Raised Oil Forecasts, 3) Midterms Preview, 4) Equities Update and 5) Week Ahead Previews 2 Nov 2026
key_insights: Goldman rates strategists argue the October rates selloff may have marked the near-term ceiling for global yields. Stress in French sovereign debt and parts of high-yield credit, plus renewed hedge value in bonds as AI-sensitive equities fell, are cited as the self-correcting forces.

Will Marshall (Chief US Rates Strategist) says the rally has only taken longer-term US yields back to around fair value, not an overshoot. He sees little evidence that real money has reduced its underweight duration position, and technical selling pressure should be smaller if yields approach the cycle highs again.

Vickie Chang (Global Macro Strategy) says US 10y1m OIS rates nearly reached 5.2% at the early-October peak, above where the market expects this hiking cycle to peak. New yield highs would need a resilient economy, a continuing AI investment boom and a path to a longer tightening cycle, and would take time.
A risk asset rebound could unwind part of the recent bond selloff and hand day-to-day rates volatility back to energy risks, according to the rates strategy view.
Goldman Commodities Research raised its Dec26 Brent forecast to $105/bbl from $90 and WTI to $94. The 2027 average forecasts rise to $88 for Brent (from $80) and $78 for WTI (from $73).

A jump in the oil risk premium to around $27 explains most of October's crude rally. Brent fair value was little changed in September and October because global inventories, its main driver, held roughly flat as adaptation rebalanced supply and demand.

The base case now includes a 1mb/d global supply disruption allowance in 2027, reflecting Mideast and Russia-Ukraine conflict risk. The forecast stays somewhat below the forwards, assuming the very high risk premium moderates and Persian Gulf output keeps recovering.

Goldman's US economics team says polling has swung about 10-11pp toward Democrats. Prediction markets imply high odds of a Democratic House majority with a margin of around 236 seats, the widest either party has had in several years.

The Senate outcome is more uncertain, with polls in decisive races inside the margin of error and a pattern of polling errors in Republican-leaning states. Goldman says the Senate matters less if Democrats win the House, since Senate passage generally needs bipartisan support and President Trump could veto legislation.

Under a Democratic majority the focus would be fiscal deadlines. Spending authority must be extended and the debt limit raised. Goldman does not expect Congress to address these before year-end and expects no major fiscal policy changes over the next two years.

Democratic proposals to reverse last year's spending cuts would add an estimated 0.25% of GDP to 2027 spending. Goldman expects tariff reversals by Democrats to be limited to a few countries or products, and expects President Trump to announce new tariff increases after the election that more than offset them, lifting the US effective tariff rate by a little under 2pp.

Goldman expects the data centre theme to fade after the election and a national moratorium to be unlikely in any outcome. It sees congressional focus shifting to AI regulation, where a compromise codifying basic federal oversight is possible but restrictive regulation is unlikely.

US Equity Derivative Sales (Coppersmith) shows the largest drop in global risk appetite since Nov 2021, but not yet at levels that signal a contrarian buying opportunity because the starting point was high.
Hedge fund gross exposure remains elevated at 314% (97th percentile over 5 years) while net exposure is in the 10th percentile over 1 year.
AI-related equity volatility has overtaken energy as a key driver of bond yields, per GS GIR.

Week ahead central bank calls: RBA 4.85% (consensus 4.85%, last 4.60%), Riksbank 2.00% (consensus 2.00%, last 1.75%), Norges Bank 4.50% hold, BoE 4.00% (consensus 4.00%, last 3.75%), Copom hold at 13.75%, Banxico hold at 6.50% with a 40% probability of a 25bp cut to 6.25%.

Payrolls on Friday: GS expects +75k vs consensus +62k (last +29k), with unemployment at 4.2% in line with consensus and the last reading. US midterms are Tuesday, with all 435 House seats, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships on the ballot.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman rates and macro strategists argue yields may have found a near-term ceiling. Stress in French sovereign debt and high-yield credit, restored bond hedge value as AI-sensitive equities fell, and a market-implied path that is hard to sustain without a longer hiking cycle all limit further upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Long-end yields have only returned to around fair value, real money's underweight duration position has barely shrunk, and the ceiling is described as near-term only. Yields could exceed the early-October peak over time.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If the economy holds up, the AI investment boom continues, and a path to a more extended tightening cycle opens up, yields could reach new highs.

tension_points.bull_case: A larger risk premium is warranted given downside risks to Mideast supply, the length of past major supply shocks and the difficulty of a lasting diplomatic breakthrough. Goldman includes a 1mb/d supply disruption allowance in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Fair value was little changed in September and October with inventories flat. The base case stays somewhat below the forwards, assuming the very high risk premium moderates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The base case assumes the very high risk premium moderates and Persian Gulf output continues its gradual recovery, so a failure of either would undercut it.
